key_insight: Greedy decoding in LLMs is not truly deterministic across numerics: BF16 and FP16 can produce different outputs from the same model, prompt, and hardware.
engineering_relevance: Inference systems that switch precision for speed or cost may change user-visible outputs, so precision choice must be treated as a correctness variable, not just a performance setting.
method: Compared BF16 vs FP16 greedy decoding on identical hardware across six models and three benchmarks.
Analyzed error propagation from body layers to the LM head using top-two logit margin and directional perturbation.
Tested selective FP32 LM-head recomputation only when the margin fell below a threshold.
evidence_signal: Across 1.1B–7B models and three benchmarks, 49–100% of prompts diverged by precision, and selective FP32 LM-head recomputation improved exact agreement by 22–36 percentage points on A10G with under 4% latency overhead in low-batch inference.
watch_item: The mitigation is partial: its benefit fades when body-layer error dominates, especially at batch size ≥8 and under end-to-end FP8.
paper_title: Greedy Decoding Is Not Precision-Invariant: Cross-Precision Output Divergence in LLM Inference
